output.brief: Analyzer B most likely had one chance QC outlier, or a one-off sampling glitch. Several things point that way: the repeat from the same vial passed, and Levels 1 and 3 and sodium and chloride were fine. There was one Westgard violation in a month, which is about what chance produces. The QC means did not move after the lot change. Patient results rerun on Analyzer A agreed within 0.02 mmol/L on average, and the patient medians were unchanged. QC ran on schedule, so the short-staffing theory is not supported. The Ward 6 high potassiums are split evenly between Analyzer A and Analyzer B. Most of them had long transport times because the tube station is down, and four overflow renal patients arrived. That points to transport delay and patient mix, not analyzer error. I did not collect any extra evidence, so the sampling-glitch cause stays unconfirmed. Recommended sign-off: do not recall results, quarantine the lot or widen limits. Return Analyzer B to service with extra Level 2 QC for a week, and close the 186 results with no amendments. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples on the high results, and fix or work around the tube station. Don't record the glitch as a confirmed cause.
